gaps.text: outside supported scope: The supplied pages cover optical spectra of chemical composition and morphology; none of them addresses line pressure or flow rate, which are hydraulic quantities, so the request as asked goes beyond that material. The only optically addressable part - an early warning of blockage from a change in the slurry at the probe - has no source support and would have to be tested first on representative samples.
Measurement of line pressure with fiber-optic or spectroscopic products.
Measurement of slurry flow rate with fiber-optic or spectroscopic products.
Detection or early warning of pipe blockage, and any warning time.

items.finding: ATR probes can be used for in-line measurements in demanding environments and in reaction mixtures containing highly oxidative or corrosive substances.
items.how_it_applies: This could support testing an ATR-based probe (O2) on a slurry transfer line, but it does not show that line pressure, flow rate or blockage can be measured.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source concerns reaction mixtures and corrosive chemicals, not a slurry in a transfer pipe; transfer to slurry solids, pipe geometry and blockage warning is unproven.

citation.quote: Attenuated total reflection probes (ATR) allow in-line measurements even in demanding measurement environments and reaction mixtures with highly oxidative and corrosive substances, such as chlorosilanes or strong acids and bases.
citation.label: E01 ¶4

items.finding: ATR-FTIR combined with PCA was reported as valuable for real-time reaction monitoring and identifying faulty batches.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests testing whether ATR-FTIR spectra plus a multivariate model can flag abnormal changes in the slurry at the probe, as a possible early-warning concept, but not as proof of blockage detection.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is about reaction monitoring and batch fault identification, not slurry flow, pipe blockage or warning time; the PCA model and sample matrix differ.

citation.quote: The combination of ATR-FTIR measurements and PCA proved to be a valuable tool for real-time reaction monitoring and identifying faulty batches.
citation.label: E01 ¶34
